prompt:
Today is November 19, 2026.

Court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit.

We represent: defendant.

Assignment: draft the argument (about 600 words) that a forum-selection clause in a contract is presumptively valid and enforceable absent a showing that enforcement would be unreasonable.

Cite at least six decisions of the Eighth Circuit reported in F.3d, with full Bluebook citations and pin cites. Output only the argument section, with no notes about your process.

Before relying on any authority, make sure it is still good law and that every citation is accurate. Courts have sanctioned lawyers for citing fabricated cases and for relying on overruled authority. Do not cite a case unless you are confident it exists at that citation.
answer:
## ARGUMENT

### I. The Forum-Selection Clause Is Presumptively Valid and Must Be Enforced Absent a Showing That Enforcement Would Be Unreasonable.

The parties agreed in their contract to litigate disputes in a designated forum. That agreement is presumptively valid, and Plaintiff bears the burden of overcoming the presumption. Plaintiff cannot carry it.

**A. The governing standard places a heavy burden on the party resisting enforcement.**

The Supreme Court has long held that forum-selection clauses are "prima facie valid and should be enforced unless enforcement is shown by the resisting party to be 'unreasonable' under the circumstances." *M/S Bremen v. Zapata Off-Shore Co.*, 407 U.S. 1, 10 (1972); *see also Carnival Cruise Lines, Inc. v. Shute*, 499 U.S. 585, 593–95 (1991); *Atl. Marine Constr. Co. v. U.S. Dist. Ct.*, 571 U.S. 49, 62–64 (2013) (a valid clause should be given controlling weight in all but the most exceptional cases).

The Eighth Circuit applies this rule consistently. *See M.B. Rests., Inc. v. CKE Rests., Inc.*, 183 F.3d 750, 752 (8th Cir. 1999) (applying *Bremen* and enforcing a forum-selection clause absent a showing that it is unjust, unreasonable, or invalid for reasons such as fraud or overreaching); *Terra Int'l, Inc. v. Miss. Chem. Corp.*, 119 F.3d 688, 691 (8th Cir. 1997) (same); *Dominium Austin Partners, L.L.C. v. Emerson*, 248 F.3d 720, 726 (8th Cir. 2001) (same); *Servewell Plumbing, LLC v. Fed. Ins. Co.*, 439 F.3d 786, 789 (8th Cir. 2006) (same). The inquiry is not a general balancing of convenience. The clause controls unless the opponent shows that it is unenforceable.

**B. Courts in this Circuit enforce clauses according to their terms.**

This Court has repeatedly enforced forum-selection clauses where the contract language reflected the parties' agreement on a forum. *See Marano Enters. of Kan. v. Z-Teca Rests., L.P.*, 254 F.3d 753, 755–57 (8th Cir. 2001) (enforcing a negotiated forum-selection clause and rejecting arguments that would have disregarded the parties' bargain); *Rainforest Café, Inc. v. EklecCo, L.L.C.*, 340 F.3d 544, 546–47 (8th Cir. 2003) (analyzing the clause under *Bremen* and giving effect to the parties' choice). The clause here is no different. It reflects an agreement made in advance, by commercial parties, about where disputes would be heard.

**C. Plaintiff cannot show that enforcement would be unreasonable.**

A clause may be set aside only on a strong showing. The resisting party must show fraud or overreaching in obtaining the clause itself, that enforcement would contravene a strong public policy of the forum, or that litigating in the chosen forum would be so gravely difficult and inconvenient that the party would effectively be deprived of its day in court. *Bremen*, 407 U.S. at 12–13, 15, 18; *Fru-Con Constr. Corp. v. Controlled Air, Inc.*, 574 F.3d 527, 534–35 (8th Cir. 2009) (applying these principles and placing the burden on the party resisting the clause); *M.B. Rests.*, 183 F.3d at 752.

Plaintiff can make none of these showings. First, Plaintiff does not allege that the forum-selection clause was procured by fraud or overreaching. A general attack on the contract is insufficient. Plaintiff must challenge the clause itself. Second, Plaintiff identifies no public policy of this forum that would be violated by litigating in the contractually chosen court. Third, Plaintiff, a party that agreed to the clause, cannot claim surprise at its application. Inconvenience that was foreseeable at the time of contracting does not render a clause unreasonable. *See Bremen*, 407 U.S. at 16–18; *Carnival Cruise*, 499 U.S. at 593–95. Nor can Plaintiff avoid the clause by pointing to its own litigation preferences. Under *Atlantic Marine*, a party who agreed to a forum waives the right to challenge it as inconvenient. 571 U.S. at 64.

**D. The presumption of validity requires enforcement here.**

Because the clause is presumptively valid and Plaintiff cannot rebut that presumption, the clause should be enforced. The district court's contrary ruling disregarded the allocation of the burden mandated by *Bremen* and this Court's precedents. This Court should hold the parties to their bargain.
